classification.difficultyReason: Direct multiplication of independent die and spinner probabilities, with simple event counts.

content.prompt:
Alison is rolling a die and spinning a spinner.
What is the probability that she gets:

spec.sourceRegion: Practice, paired die and square spinner
spec.description: Die on the left; square spinner on the right divided by its diagonals, with A top, B right, C bottom and D left. Decorative fills omitted.
spec.mathematics: Six equally likely die outcomes and four equally likely spinner outcomes. Die visible faces show 3, 6 and 2.

children.label: a
children.prompt: 1 on the die and C on the spinner.

children.label: b
children.prompt: An even number and a consonant.

answer.worked:
The even numbers are 2, 4 and 6; the consonants are B, C and D.
$$\begin{aligned}P(\text{even, consonant})&=\frac36\times\frac34\\&=\frac9{24}\\&=\frac38\end{aligned}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: A number greater than 4 and a vowel.

answer.worked:
The numbers greater than 4 are 5 and 6; the only vowel is A.
$$\begin{aligned}P(>4,\text{ vowel})&=\frac26\times\frac14\\&=\frac2{24}\\&=\frac1{12}\end{aligned}$$
